source.title: Detecting and Characterizing Planning in Language Models
source.authors: Jatin Nainani; Sankaran Vaidyanathan; Connor Watts; Andre N. Assis; Alice Rigg

page_placements.theme: Post-training (RLHF, instruction tuning) and commitment to a response-level plan

record.tranche_reason: The study refines the definition of planning and reports results that challenge its universality: Gemma-2-2B Instruct improvises on the rhyme task, while code-generation behavior varies between planning and improvisation.
record.gate_note: The authors cite findings from prior work on Claude 3.5 Haiku and future-token probing; those cited results are not recorded as this study’s results. Values used to select thresholds or features are not rows. Rows below are the study’s own poem, code-task, and base-versus-instruct results.
record.test_reason: The study applies FTE plus precursor-influence steering to Gemma-2-2B. It reruns the Lindsey et al. rhyme prompt and finds improvisation, not planning (V4, V6). It also tests look-ahead in MBPP code generation and finds planning in some cases but not others (V5, V6). It uses a different method (GemmaScope SAE circuits and steering) aimed at the same question, and its results argue the rhyme-planning finding does not carry over.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors also conclude planning can be done poorly: models plan toward incorrect targets or fail to choose among competing plans. They also report no clear rule for when Gemma plans versus improvises.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE-feature future-token readout and negative steering, with a circuit-discovery and cluster-level detection pipeline. It is not a direct replication of the original Claude attribution-graph procedure, though it tests the same rhyme example and causal-planning idea.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on task and forward pass: the poem prompt shows no planning circuit, code tasks include planning, improvisation, and ambiguous cases, and the Base model can target a different token from Instruct.

fits_no_version.finding: Base-model pass rates are 54% on tasks where Instruct planned and 100% on tasks where it improvised. The authors read this as instruction tuning refining plan selection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruction tuning improves plan target selection rather than creating planning.

record.problems: The study is limited to Gemma-2-2B Base and Instruct, one rhyme prompt, and a subset of MBPP. The authors note possible mismatch from applying Base-trained SAEs to Instruct, reliance on MLP-attached SAEs, polysemantic latents, and degenerate steering outputs that make some cases ambiguous. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported numeric or explicit result-bearing conditions were omitted.

untested.parts: No frontier model is tested; Claude results are only cited.
Not tested as stated. The study gives no accuracy of predicting future tokens from a single hidden state; FTE is a top-10 logit-lens check on selected SAE latents.
The study does not distinguish pre-caching from breadcrumbs, or test why early features are computed.
Only Gemma-2-2B Instruct on one rhyme prompt; no other open models; no attribution-graph tool.
Multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban and other architectures are not tested; only MBPP code is.

missing.what: Planning prevalence: of 60 MBPP tasks, the Instruct model was classified planning on 13 and improvising on 11 (24 classified); the rest were neither or can't say.
Instruct counterfactual: suppressing the 'digits'/'sort' plan in Instruct reproduces the Base model's failed answer.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. There is no uncertainty reporting, and the case studies are hand-selected. The SAEs were trained on the Base model and applied to Instruct. Appendix B.2 lists steering token '1' where §3.2.2 says '2'.

versions.untested_parts: The version specifies a frontier model; this study tests Gemma-2-2B, not a frontier model.
The study tests Logit-Lens top-10 encoding for selected tokens and positions, not general prediction accuracy across tokens, horizons, layers, or models.
The study does not establish why the features are computed, or whether their early activity is specifically due to later utility rather than another mechanism.
Only Gemma-2-2B Instruct is tested on the rhyme task; the study does not test other open-weight models or attribution-graph tools.
The study tests MBPP code generation, not multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or other architectures.
The study does not establish that all apparent planning is local or heuristic; its code examples include causal effects on intermediate tokens.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Applied the FTE and PI pipeline to predictions in the rhyming-couplet completion; manually inspected the circuit for predicting “habit”.

conditions.value: approximately 26k latents; at least 60% logit recovery

rows.measure: Whether any circuit met both future-token encoding and precursor-influence criteria; timing of causal relevance of features associated with “habit”.
rows.value: No circuit met both criteria. Latents writing to “habit” became causally relevant only at the final token; early negative steering did not change intermediate tokens as reported for the comparison study.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as improvisation from local phonetic and thematic cues rather than an early rhyme plan.
rows.check: State is relative to the version. For V4 the effect is absent: no circuit met FTE+PI, and 'habit' latents mattered only at the final token. For V6 the effect is observed: the authors attribute the rhyme to local phonetic and thematic cues. Remove V3, since the study does not test why features are computed.

source_check.correct: V4: absent. V6: observed. No circuit satisfied both FTE and PI; habit-writing latents became causally relevant only at the final token.
source_check.problem: The shared observed state is correct for V6 but incorrect for V4.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Negatively steered the earliest feature encoding future token “1” while predicting a comma.

conditions.value: sort a list of tuples by the second value
“1”, ym = 305; ranked first among top-10 logits
negative steering; coefficient not stated in §3.2.1

rows.measure: Future-token encoding and effect of steering on the next token, intermediate continuation, and future-token appearance.
rows.baseline: comma followed by the continuation that uses key=lambda x: x[1]
rows.value: Next token changed to a closing parenthesis; generation added a newline and ended the function; “1” did not appear in the continuation.
rows.note: The steered generation failed the unit test.
rows.check: Planning was observed for V5, so V6 is reversed here; the shared state is set to V5. Remove V2 and V3. FTE here is a logit-lens projection of a selected SAE decoder direction (top-10), not prediction of future tokens from a hidden state. Nothing tests pre-caching versus breadcrumbs. The horizon is short (target 8 tokens after the current token).

source_check.correct: V5: observed. For V6, causal steering contradicts the incidental-feature alternative; it does not establish the absence of shallow planning. Appendix B.1 gives coefficient -80.
source_check.problem: A shared observed state obscures the different implications for V5 and the two alternatives in V6.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Negatively steered the earliest feature encoding future token “2” during generation of a closed-form tetrahedral-number formula.

conditions.value: first opening bracket of the formula, yn = 180
negative steering; coefficient -80 in Appendix B.2

rows.measure: Future-token encoding and effect of steering on the next token, intermediate continuation, and future-token appearance.
rows.value: “tet” replaced the opening parenthesis as the next token; continuation formed tetrahedral_number(n-1) + 1; “2” did not appear.
rows.note: The steered generation failed the unit tests.
rows.check: Same as R2: observed for V5, reversed for V6. Remove V2 and V3. Appendix B.2 lists the steering token as '1' with coeff -80, while §3.2.2 says '2'. This internal inconsistency should be flagged.

source_check.correct: §3.2.2 and Figure 2B identify target 2; Appendix B.2 identifies steering token 1 with coefficient -80. V5: observed; the causal result contradicts V6's incidental-feature alternative, without establishing a horizon distribution.
source_check.problem: The source contradicts itself about the steering target, and the shared state does not distinguish the linked versions.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Negatively steered the feature encoding future token “sort” while predicting “digits”.

conditions.value: form the largest number from a list of digits
layer 17, t = 190, first tab after the docstring
negative steering; coefficient -60 in Appendix B.3

rows.measure: Future-token encoding and effect of steering on the next token, intermediate continuation, and future-token appearance.
rows.baseline: generation sorts the digits and constructs the number in reverse order
rows.value: Next token changed from “digits” to “max”; continuation began max_num = and did not contain “sort”.
rows.note: The steered program failed all hidden tests.
rows.check: Observed for V5, reversed for V6. Remove V2 and V3. The target 'sort' is only about 2 tokens ahead ('digits.sort'), so the horizon is shallow.

source_check.correct: §3.2.3 gives current position 191 and feature position 190; Appendix B.3 labels its prefix as ending at token 311 and gives coefficient -60. V5: observed; causal steering contradicts V6's incidental-feature alternative but remains compatible with shallow planning.
source_check.problem: Main-text and appendix prefix positions disagree; the shared state hides the distinction between causal and shallow planning.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Steered features encoding future token “for” during the divisor-check expression.

conditions.value: return tuples whose elements are all divisible by k

rows.measure: Future-token encoding and effect of steering on the continuation.
rows.baseline: generation completes “== 0 for element in tup)” and returns matching tuples
rows.value: Output collapsed around the divisor check into text like “, k):” and lost the generator expression, producing a syntactically invalid snippet.
rows.note: The authors classify this as can’t say because the target token is in the input and the steered output is degenerate.
rows.check: Remove V2 and V3. The target is in the prompt and the output is degenerate; the authors label it can't say.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Steered features encoding future token “-” while predicting “num”.

conditions.value: form the largest number from a list of digits

rows.measure: Future-token encoding and effect of steering on the continuation.
rows.baseline: generation sorts the list and builds the number by concatenating digits in reverse order
rows.value: Steered output became degenerate, beginning with digits = len(digits) and followed by stray triple-quoted lines.
rows.note: The authors classify this as can’t say because the intervention produced degenerate output.
rows.check: Remove V2 and V3. Degenerate steered output.

source_check.locator_found: §3.2.4, Largest number from digits; Appendix C.2

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Steered features encoding future token “(” during a different tetrahedral-number forward pass.

conditions.value: “(”, already present in the function signature and assertions

rows.measure: Future-token encoding and effect of steering on the continuation.
rows.value: Steered generation became a stream of “the” and “The” tokens.
rows.note: The authors classify this as can’t say because the target overlaps the prompt and the intervention produced degenerate output.
rows.check: Remove V2 and V3. Prompt overlap and degenerate output.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B Base
rows.operation_detail: Detected plans for both “2” and an alternative “-”; suppressed the “-” features.
rows.measure: Future-token encoding and effect of suppressing the competing target on the generated formula.
rows.baseline: when following the incorrect plan, the model generates 1+2(n-1)
rows.value: Suppressing the “-” target caused the model to return the correct formula, n*(n+1)*(n+2)/6.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as evidence that the base model plans, but selects between competing targets less effectively.
rows.check: Remove V2 and V3. The base model plans toward two competing targets, and suppressing '-' recovers the correct formula. Observed for V5, reversed for V6. The coefficient is not stated.

source_check.correct: V5: observed. Suppressing the competing minus-token features restores the correct formula. This contradicts V6's incidental-feature alternative; the passage does not quantify the planning horizon.
source_check.problem: The shared observed state does not distinguish evidence for planning from evidence against V6's incidental-feature alternative.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B Base
rows.operation_detail: Applied the planning-detection pipeline to identify the model’s future target in the largest-number task.

conditions.value: form the largest number from a list of digits
Instruct plans for “digits”; Base plans for “max”

rows.measure: Future-token encoding and whether the selected target leads to the correct answer.
rows.baseline: Instruct targets “digits” and sorts the list
rows.value: Base targets “max”, does not have “digits” as a potential plan, and fails to return a correct answer.
rows.note: The study reports the Base target and failure; this passage does not report an intervention on the Base model.
rows.check: The base model is reported as planning, just toward the wrong target ('max'). Planning itself is observed, not partial. Remove V2, V3 and V6: no intervention on the base model is reported, so the study gives no V6 result here.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B Base
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated task-pass rates on MBPP tasks grouped by the Instruct model’s planning classification.
rows.note: The comparison is conditioned on the Instruct model’s task classifications.
rows.check: This is a task pass rate on a subset selected by the Instruct model's labels. It measures capability, not look-ahead in the base model, so it should not link to any version.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B Base
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated task-pass rates on MBPP tasks grouped by the Instruct model’s improvisation classification.
rows.note: The comparison is conditioned on the Instruct model’s task classifications.
rows.check: Same as R10: a capability pass rate on a selection-conditioned subset, not a planning measure.

Base pass rates are capability comparisons on subsets selected using Instruct, not direct planning prevalence estimates.

statements.correction: R2: current position 297, target position 305, earliest feature position 294. R3: current position 180, earliest feature position 18; target 2 in §3.2.2 versus steering token 1 in Appendix B.2. R4: current position 191, earliest feature position 190. R8: suppressing minus-token features restores the correct formula. No planning-horizon distribution reported.
